criteria.durable_checkpointed: Adopt a finite durable fanout contract for both cohort spellings: the trigger commits a fanout intent with a frozen cohort cutoff; each member becomes an independently admitted child occurrence with its own receipt and bounded transaction; a durable checkpoint records completed children so crash recovery resumes without re-executing them. Concurrently deleted children record skipped outcomes; one child's rejection never rolls back siblings; supersession marks undispatched children skipped. Zero draft edits at all four sites. Price: the largest implementation cost — new durable intent type, checkpoint table, recovery scan, per-child receipt correlation, T24 atomic fanout-intent staging, and a full T34 proof (499/500/501/1000 completeness, crash resume, duplicate replay, concurrent change, rejected children, retry, supersession). Strongest opposing case: mini-workflow-engine machinery for four sites whose failure modes (lost checkpoints, repeated children, misreported partials) are exactly the audit's worries — if real cohorts stay small, bounded atomicity proves the same workflows far cheaper, and no evidenced cohort needs cross-crash durability.
criteria.bounded_atomic: Adopt each= as in-transaction bounded iteration: trigger plus all children commit atomically in one owner transaction under a hard cohort cap (the limit=100 order is already used in-draft); overflow rejects the trigger; a crash retries the whole occurrence as one unit with receipt replay. No frozen cutoff beyond the transaction snapshot; no per-child receipts or outcome reporting; only whole-occurrence supersession. Zero draft edits if all real cohorts fit the cap. Price: cheapest adoption, but the cap is the cost — all-or-nothing over a whole model is a transaction-size hazard (one contested row aborts a large sweep, retry storms follow), Shift whole-model sweeps fit only if Commitment/Swap populations stay small, and atomicity changes observable behavior (no partial completion exists). Strongest opposing case: the cap that saves the engine strands the very Shift sweeps the drafts wrote as whole-model traversals; authors will bump limit= until the bound is fiction; and nothing in the drafts pins atomic-versus-per-child outcomes.
criteria.no_primitive: Keep each= rejected (E1203 retained): no fanout primitive, no language cohort concept. Authors express traversal with existing bounded forms (explicit queries plus per-record operations or bounded for-limit loops) with completeness riding ordinary per-operation receipts; multi-step sweeps are separate operations with separate receipts. The T33 decision becomes explicit scoping with a supported remodeling idiom. Price: zero language and runtime cost, but maximum per-site migration and review cost at all four sites under draft-owner adjudication (filter parity for null-or-match guards, parent.parent navigation, schedule-key pairing, per-signup notice uniqueness each need a witness), repeated for every future sweep; T34 becomes a scoping record. Strongest opposing case: it answers a completeness problem by deleting the completeness obligation — mid-sweep inserts silently missed, mid-sweep failures silently partial, plain traversal intent rewritten into verbose plumbing — while the R19 flip burden demands a continuation design with EQUAL completeness and recovery, not merely fewer features.
criteria.anchored_only: Adopt the durable checkpointed machinery but scope the cohort language to parent-anchored collections (event.opportunity.Signup and equivalents): the cutoff freezes the pinned parent's collection at trigger commit, with per-child receipts, version-guarded admission, per-child retry, and undispatched-only supersession inside each adopted cohort. Bare-model traversals keep E1203 until an authoritative whole-model coverage contract exists — partial adoption with an explicit deferred remainder that never promises whole-model directory coverage. Volunteer site 4 checks unchanged; site 3's parent-id filter is already an anchored sweep in disguise. Price: full machinery cost (checkpoint, recovery, per-child receipts) but T34 proof covers anchored cohorts only; adds a two-tier cohort language to teach and diagnose; Shift sites 1-2 stay blocked unless remodeled. Strongest opposing case: it ships the machinery while stranding the harder half — Shift's eligibility sweeps, the primary R19 sites, stay blocked because no single anchor covers all five emitters, so the project pays full costs for scoping outcomes on the flagship workflow, and the anchored/bare split reads as arbitrary checker strictness.

fanout_rule.instructions: For the fanout gate, which rule delivers the required cohort, checkpoint, identity, failure and supersession semantics at the lowest total cost — implementation plus T34 proof plus migration plus re-proof — without deleting the completeness obligation the drafts state? Judge every option under the same cost accounting; machinery, proof burden, migration churn, and future-sweep repetition all count.

request.state: The T33 fanout gate decides cohort/checkpoint/identity/concurrent-change/failure/supersession semantics for four each= fanout sites currently rejected with E1203 (R19, bucket d, medium confidence): Shift review_commitment (bare-model Commitment sweep with null-or-match filters), Shift review_swap (bare-model Swap sweep with parent.parent navigation plus an invalidation predicate), Volunteer refresh_reminders (bare-model Signup sweep filtered to one opportunity, schedule cancel/re-arm), Volunteer cancel_signup (parent-anchored event.opportunity.Signup sweep, guarded per-signup email). The acceptance bar has four items: the Shift eligibility sweep, the Volunteer reminder refresh, the Volunteer cancellation sweep with retry-safe per-signup notice, and the negatives (unsupported spellings stay blocked with a diagnostic; partial execution is never reported complete; ordinary bounded loops still reject overflow; no silent whole-model traversal where the cohort contract is unadopted). Shift and Volunteer are ACCEPTED-WORKFLOW-INTENT with R19 as the T33-gated blocker; T40 qualifies them only on adopted T34. Settled context all options share: T24 COMPLETE (atomic trigger-commit/outbox-staging join, claim/record/requeue/reconcile/sweep execution, proven on memory plus miniflare-D1 plus workerd-DO); T28-A adopted (imported-parent reads enroll in the same-owner fence); T32a checkpoint_fence ADOPTED and fence-plus-wire LANDED (commit-time revision re-assertion plus permission and revocation re-evaluation, executor guards, rejected-receipt rule, transitive fresh scopes; cloudflare integration in flight; narrower per-team/per-record fence still open); committed-event immutability with per-occurrence receipt replay; per-row batch precedent; bounded exports never labeling incomplete data complete. Measured unknowns bounding every option: NO draft example pins snapshot-vs-live membership, concurrent insert/move/remove handling, or re-trigger-during-flight for any site (absence confirmed by re-read, so the gate picks defaults without draft grounding); the largest observed cohort-adjacent count is 2 records while 499/500/501/1000 are audit-plan proof obligations, not observed needs; no single parent anchor covers all five EligibilityReview emitters (roster supplied by 2 of 5; employee is an imported type, location a text id, account a user record — none a traversable collection); each= spelling comparison is ordered AFTER the completeness contract is concrete. This is a design choice, not a measured implementation result.
